subject: physics
question_text: What is the function of the sunshield of a space telescope such as the James Webb Space Telescope? Name the branch of physics its working belongs to.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 14 Very Short Answer Question 12 (printed p.144). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: the sunshield blocks incoming heat and light and radiates the absorbed heat away, keeping the mirror near a few tens of kelvin, which is genuinely needed to detect faint infrared light; the branch named is thermal physics (heat radiation) together with optics, not electromagnetism.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Function of the sunshield
lines: It blocks the heat and light of
the Sun, Earth and Moon, and
steps.why: The mirror must detect very faint infrared light from distant objects. Any warmth in the mirror itself would radiate infrared light of its own, adding to the faint signal being measured, so the sunshield keeps the mirror and instruments at a few tens of kelvin.
common_mistakes: Saying the sunshield protects the telescope, with no mention of heat or temperature.
Describing it as shade for astronauts, confusing it with a crewed spacecraft.
steps.memory_tip: Sunshield blocks heat, radiates it away, keeps the mirror cold enough to see faint infrared light.
steps.margin_note: A numeric value near a few tens of kelvin is accepted; an exact figure is not required.

steps.label: Branch of physics
lines: and radiates it away, and the
steps.why: Blocking incoming heat and radiating it away is a thermal physics problem, while forming a sharp image on the mirror is an optics problem, so the sunshield and the telescope together use both branches.
common_mistakes: Naming only space physics, which is not a recognised branch.
Naming electromagnetism alone, without heat radiation or optics.
steps.memory_tip: Heat radiating away is thermal physics; forming the image is optics — the telescope needs both.
steps.margin_note: Thermal physics is the branch behind how the shield itself works. Optics belongs in the full answer because the shield exists to protect the telescope's optics, not because optics alone describes the shield's working.
